newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mixed Monday, with the complex consolidating after losses Friday.
But a sharply higher U.S. dollar, following the Socialist party's win in France's elections over the weekend would limit any gains for the complex, analysts said.

Nervousness about the possibly imminent resumption in platinum group metals exports by Russia would also limit gains in platinum group metals, after officials of Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, arrived in Japan on the weekend to begin talks on a supply contract.
COMEX August gold, now the active contract, was seen opening unchanged to down 50 cents an ounce from Friday's close at $347.50.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $344.20/70 an ounce, compared to the London Monday morning fix at $344.00 and the New York close Friday around $344.40/90.
COMEX gold stocks fell 96 ounces Friday to 868,169 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks were up 466,758 ounces to 200,196,865 ounces.
COMEX July silver was seen opening up 1.00 to 2.00 cents from Friday's close at $4.675.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from the previous close at $401.20 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents also from Friday's close at $173.00.
